build_to.name: PaperBomb
build_to.silhouette: clean octagon - four straight sides, four straight 45 deg chamfers; no tear, no nick, no dog-ear (REFERENCE_SPEC section 1)

sockets.name: Face
sockets.use: decal, glow and VFX anchor on the printed face (the tag rests on its curl, not on this point)

sockets.name: Attach
sockets.use: stick to a wall, glue to a crate, parent to a kunai

sockets.name: Fuse
sockets.use: spark and burn VFX start; the _M green scorch gradient radiates from here

sockets.name: Cord
sockets.use: ties to the kunai's Ring socket at (-103.5, 0, 0) mm; also a fuse cord

provenance.design: the user's own design; tracing and sampling it is the method

elements.corners: drawn (traced shapes ready: group 'frame', contour part)
elements.rules: drawn (traced strokes ready: group 'frame', stroke part)
elements.columns: typeset from MasaFont-Bold.ttf (traced shapes ready: groups 'col_*'; waits for the font result)

front.method: edge-extended on the far edge; the card origin is untouched

back.method: edge-extended on the far edge; the card origin is untouched

ornaments.colour: red scroll + knob + dart, after RG; nothing outboard of the side rules

ring_runs.note: a dry lap and one run per angle pull against each other: a bare streak crossing the whole stroke splits it in two at that angle. The gate is that MOST angles are a single run and that the runs are as wide as the study's stroke, not that every angle is one.

relief_bands.study: fibre grain 0.010 - 0.020 mm relief on a 0.1 - 0.4 mm cell

ink_over_rules.note: the centre character crosses the ring by design and is excluded; what is counted is ink over the FRAME

leaf_zone.reference: RG: 58.99 mm2 of ink, ALL black, 0.00 red - it is the glyph's foot

ink_halo.reference: RG 0.51 mm (its own 1 px floor); HR character 0.11 - 0.23 mm

outline.source: props_lib.paperbomb_art.card_outline_mm - the same polyline the texture is cut to

octagon.reference: REFERENCE_SPEC rows S2/S7/S8/S10 - the reference tag is a clean octagon: 1820 boundary samples, worst 0.20 mm, zero runs inboard

atlas.back_island_note: the study's 0.458 would have overlapped the front raster's padding by 15 px; the island is the same size and density

transfer_verification.method: Cycles EMIT bake of the front art sampled through a temporary CardUV layer onto UV0, on a throwaway copy of LOD0

how_each_channel_is_made.BC / ORM.G / N / M: TRANSFERRED: the art rasters are the atlas's own pixel grid (same px/mm, integer offset, no rotation), so the move is a 1:1 blit and a Cycles pass could only resample it. Proved by transfer_verification, which is a real bake through a different UV mapping.
how_each_channel_is_made.ORM.R: BAKED: a Cycles ambient-occlusion bake of the LOD0 shell onto UV0.
how_each_channel_is_made.ORM.B: constant 0 - paper is not a metal anywhere on the card.

collision.shape: containing octagonal prism (eight supporting half-planes in plan)
collision.naming_rule: UCX_<render mesh NODE name>_00; the node is SM_PaperBomb_LOD0 after make_lod_group, and UCX_SM_PaperBomb_00 on it would import with convex count 0 and no collision at all

kunai_dry_fit.note: both sockets are identity, so mating is a pure translation and the tag's +X (the top of the card) runs along the kunai's +X - the tag hangs off the butt with its top at the ring, which is what a cord through a pommel ring does.  A non-identity Cord would rotate the whole tag here, which is what the first build shipped.
kunai_dry_fit.summary: Cord +X out of the top, mates to Ring by translation [-184.4, 0.0, 4.0] mm; tag spans X -265.4 to -103.4 mm against the kunai's -119.5 to 160.5 mm

skin.note: min / max are single edges and are dominated by chord-against-arc where the mesh polygonises a tight bend; p01 / p99 are the texture-stretch claim

self_intersections.note: front/back skin pairs that cross; an AO bake reads each one as a near-black UV cell with straight, axis-aligned edges

front.note: camera up is +X (the top of the tag); camera right is -Y (the right of the print)

back.note: the card is turned 180 deg about its long axis; the camera and lamps do not move

wire.camera: the hero camera and framing, flat-lit

persp.note: low, near end-on: the curl, the two creases and the dog-ear in silhouette - the shot that says this is paper and not a decal

lodgrind.note: one render per LOD at a third of the frame width under the hero rig, captions parented to the camera, stitched

relief.note: measured on a DIAGNOSTIC pair under a 6 deg key nearly opposite the camera, not on the shipped close-up: that arrangement makes the normal map modulate the specular lobe, which is the loudest test of whether the map is connected and doing work, and is also exactly the lighting that veiled the ink in the first build's gallery image.  standard deviation of a 3 px high-pass over the object, the same frame rendered with and without the Normal input connected

luminance.band_note: the study's band scaled by this policy's paper stored luma over the 0.7965 it was calibrated on; see object_p50_band
